clinicalPearls: A rare placoid inflammatory chorioretinopathy considered to sit on a spectrum between APMPPE and serpiginous choroiditis (hence 'ampiginous')
Characterised by numerous placoid lesions, often more than fifty over the disease course, involving both posterior pole and periphery
Follows a prolonged, relapsing course over months rather than the self-limiting behaviour of classic APMPPE
Lesions show the typical early hypofluorescence and late staining of placoid disease on fluorescein angiography
Vision can be preserved but is threatened by foveal involvement and recurrent activity
Long-term immunosuppression is often required to control the relentless course
reference.pathophysiology: The condition is an idiopathic inflammatory disorder of the choriocapillaris and overlying retinal pigment epithelium, producing placoid lesions similar to those of acute posterior multifocal placoid pigment epitheliopathy and serpiginous choroiditis. Unlike self-limiting APMPPE, the inflammatory process recurs relentlessly, generating a large number of lesions across the fundus over an extended period, with choriocapillaris hypoperfusion contributing to the angiographic and imaging findings.
additionalDifferentials: Acute posterior multifocal placoid pigment epitheliopathy
additionalInvestigations: Fundus autofluorescence to map active and healed lesions
Optical coherence tomography for outer-retinal and RPE changes
Workup to exclude tuberculosis and syphilis before immunosuppression
Serial wide-field imaging to monitor the relapsing course
redFlags: Foveal or peripapillary lesions threatening central vision
reference.prognosis: The course is protracted with repeated relapses, but with sustained immunosuppression many eyes retain useful vision unless the fovea is repeatedly involved.
pitfalls: Assuming a self-limiting APMPPE course and undertreating
Starting immunosuppression before excluding tuberculosis and syphilis
Underestimating relapse risk on stopping therapy
Overlooking peripheral lesions by examining only the posterior pole
